summary: The enterprise and organization repository-level Copilot usage metrics reports now show what happens to Copilot code review feedback. A new copilot_code_review object on each repos-1-day row reports how many Copilot-reviewed pull requests merged without a later change request from a person and how many Copilot code review comments developers acted on.
takeaways: These fields show whether developers act on Copilot code review feedback in each repository, which kinds of comments land, whether custom instructions, skills, and MCP servers make a difference, and whether reviewers still request changes after Copilot reviews.

Bot pull requests: Copilot usually doesn’t evaluate comments on pull requests opened by bots, such as Copilot cloud agent. total_merged_no_human_change_request_after_review still includes those pull requests.
Counted on merge: Comments are evaluated when their pull request merges, so they count on the merge day, not the day Copilot posted them.
